policy_findings.rationale: The design keeps dependent work behind approved, reviewed plan bytes. Historical proof only revalidates the original reviewed subject (exact message, path set, retained blobs, gate/settlement) against an immutable first-parent candidate; it never treats a later descendant as reviewed. Changed governing documents (prd.md, task design.md, numbered phase design.md) are classified before any adoption and are explicitly excluded from baseline adoption even when an implementation result is their newest projection owner, so an edited plan cannot be adopted into successor authority; the routes are exact restore, same-position recovery under fresh production/counter-review/constitution review/human gate, or the existing human-owned backward restart to the owning document. The recovery action stays in the same phase_instance and re-enters produce/running rather than advancing, and the generalized cutoff over restart_history plus milestone_recovery_history prevents byte-identical reproduction from reviving invalidated design authority (repo: src/state/restart-authority.ts currently derives cutoffs from restart_history only, consistent with the described extension). The retained-behavior list also preserves the no-code-before-approved-phase-design boundary.
policy_findings.trigger_evidence: The design changes when a design milestone counts as complete and when a successor implementation handoff becomes available ("Governing-document drift" section, control-flow steps 2-3 and 7, and the recovery causes "milestone-proof-missing"/"governing-document-drift").

policy_findings.rationale: No authority is inferred. Human and authenticated no-wait modes stay distinct and requires_human_confirmation keeps its meaning at the commit action. Settlement re-pins the target and recomputes the full drift subject (target ref, complete changed/deleted path set, observed digests, committed/uncommitted classification) under the task lock, refusing materially stale choices; treating an unrelated descendant that leaves that exact subject identical as non-stale still binds the decision to the exact bytes being decided about, so the human decision remains tied to its artifact subject. The stale-gate refresh explicitly fabricates no cancellation, adoption, restore, or human provenance: it records only gate_id/kind/reason/revision, preserves the immutable request and any archived decision, and is forbidden from earning an approval or baseline-adoption record. Recovery is a fail-closed backward re-entry that invalidates prior authority via a cutoff and requires the normal approval or rule settlement again before a milestone can be committed; it grants nothing. New no-wait settlements persist milestone_target_ref/milestone_baseline_commit so authority is not derived from whichever branch is checked out, and old evidence without a durable target is never given an invented one.
policy_findings.trigger_evidence: The design alters gate subject binding and settlement revalidation for baseline-adoption, adds a server-owned stale-gate supersession, and adds a no-submission recover-milestone-authority action ("Baseline adoption and restore" and "Same-position milestone recovery").

policy_findings.rationale: Failure and uncertainty stay visible with a safe next action. Missing objects or Git command failures are classified unverifiable rather than absence; a content-preserving rewrite with no committable delta returns an explicit inspection naming two concrete remedies instead of an empty synthetic commit or a false completion; ordinary branch advancement no longer dead-ends on inspection. Adoption copy states plainly that keeping current versions performs no counter-review and grants no commit authorization, that uncommitted adopted bytes are recoverable only to the last committed repository and durable workflow boundary, and that restore may lose uncommitted versions. Governing-document drift explains why adoption is unavailable. No inspection response requires authenticated state edits.
policy_findings.trigger_evidence: The design defines terminal and non-success responses: unverifiable Git failures, the content-preserving rewritten-history inspection, and adoption/restore human copy ("Content-preserving rewritten history", "Human-facing consequences").

policy_findings.rationale: Evidence stays bound to the exact task and subject bytes and fails closed. Candidate selection is limited to the first first-parent commit after the exact authorized baseline on the authorized target — no scanning of other refs or the object database — and the original exact validator (parent, message, sorted path set including both rename endpoints, retained blob/mode identity, deletions/rename sources absent, matching gate or settlement) runs against that immutable candidate, with ancestry and ref re-resolution after tree reads. Design milestones keep the task-root confinement and unauthorized-task-document checks. The autonomous validator authenticates the candidate state.json in its own commit-tree view and requires the corresponding settlement to remain present and eligible in current state, rather than accepting a byte comparison that later append-only records would break. Recovery and supersession records carry phase_instance, subject_digest, target facts, and revisions; offers are bound to exact state revision, repository identity, target ref/head, subject, and cause, and are revalidated under the task lock. Task isolation, canonical state validation, and digest binding are listed as unchanged.
policy_findings.trigger_evidence: The design adds new durable records (milestone_recovery_history, gate_supersessions), new settlement fields, and a candidate-commit resolver that reads historical trees ("Historical milestone proof", "Durable authority changes").

summary: The reviewed design defines one implementation phase for recoverable free-form repository changes. Historical milestone proof validates the original authorized first-parent commit on the authorized target while current baseline reconciliation independently handles later output drift. Ordinary descendants preserve completion; applicable changed outputs require exact human adoption or restore without being called reviewed. Governing PRD and design documents are classified by successor consumption at every handoff, including when co-produced by implementation, and must be restored or receive owning review before dependent work advances. Representable missing proof enters fresh authority with durable cutoffs; content-preserving rewritten history with no committable delta returns an explicit safe inspection instead of an empty commit. Baseline decisions bind paths, digests, and committedness, disclose uncommitted clone limits, tolerate unrelated descendants with the same decision subject, and refresh genuinely stale interfaces. The single phase updates contracts, state and gate transactions, semantic actions, skills, maintained documentation, and focused real-Git and end-to-end tests. Independent counter-review and constitution review completed with no findings.
